name: Coalesce
label: Hydra Head
lede: A Kansas City band that started out as straight edge hardcore, broke up three times in five years, and left behind a run of records other metal bands still cite as a starting point.

eras.title: Three Kansas bands, one name change
eras.text: Sean Ingram, Jes Steineger and Stacy Hilt came out of Kansas City's straight edge and Krishnacore scene and started as Breach. They changed the name to Coalesce, recorded an EP in a day and went on the road.

years.h: Steineger and Hilt start Breach with drummer Jim Redd
years.p: [[Jes Steineger|010f7911-1f05-408f-a26f-af35631b15ab]] and [[Stacy Hilt|4f8d8b03-a215-40ad-be04-94d8003f9fb5]] had played in the Krishnacore band Amara. Drummer Jim Redd came from an alternative metal band called Loathe.

years.h: Sean Ingram comes home from Syracuse and joins
years.p: [[Sean Ingram|1170e906-848e-4769-8354-c3c0684511a2]] had left Kansas City on Christmas Day 1993 for Syracuse, New York, drawn by Earth Crisis and vegan straight edge. He wrote lyrics for the band and took over vocals.

years.h: Breach becomes Coalesce
years.p: The band changed its name to avoid confusion with a Swedish band that had the same one, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: 002 EP, cut in one day with Ed Rose
years.p: The first release was recorded in a single day at Red House Studios in Lawrence with producer Ed Rose, who would go on to record most of the band's catalog.

years.h: First U.S. tour, opening for Bloodlet and 108
years.p: Coalesce hit the road behind the EP with two heavier hardcore bands and returned to Kansas with the lineup already fraying.

eras.title: Fired, rehired, and suddenly great
eras.text: The band split in March 1996 and re-formed four months later with a new drummer, then made the records that defined its sound. Everything ran on Kansas City labels and a lot of tape.

years.cap: The four-piece that made Give Them Rope
years.h: Band breaks up mid-audition after Jim Redd pushes Ingram out
years.p: Drummer Jim Redd and Sean Ingram clashed in March 1996, and Redd persuaded the others to drop Ingram. The band folded while [[James DeWees|24ff2fe2-c61c-4002-b717-444ffa811515]] was auditioning for the vocal spot.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's account is that personality clashes between Ingram and Redd ended the band, with Redd convincing the others to oust Ingram, and that DeWees showed up to audition as a possible new vocalist.

In July 1996 Steineger called Ingram and the band re-formed, with DeWees on drums. Redd did not come back because he was attending the University of Maryland.

years.h: Steineger calls Ingram, DeWees moves behind the drums
years.p: [[James DeWees|24ff2fe2-c61c-4002-b717-444ffa811515]], who came in to audition as a vocalist, ended up as the new drummer.

years.h: Give Them Rope arrives on Edison Recordings
years.p: Eleven songs and about forty minutes of metalcore recorded at Red House with Ed Rose, and the record fans still hold up as the band's first peak.

years.h: Split 7-inch with [[The Get Up Kids|1b54e90c-638e-4fdd-a20e-4ab09db9fdaf]]
years.p: Coalesce also put out split singles with The Get Up Kids, Today Is the Day and Converge around this time.

years.h: Stacy Hilt leaves, and Nathan Ellis joins on bass
years.p: Hilt quit, Wikipedia says because he was exhausted by how hard the band played live. [[Nathan Ellis|c5ef22ff-6712-4f68-9b4b-53871a6c29c4]] took over on bass.

years.h: Functioning on Impatience: seven songs, about 20 minutes
years.p: Recorded at Red House with Ed Rose and released through Second Nature Recordings, with a rib-cage cover shot by photographer Carrie Whitney.

years.h: Split with [[Boy Sets Fire|ba561cc7-2050-47d3-8bc2-c645a1393d90]]
years.p: The band shared a split 7-inch with Boy Sets Fire, the Delaware hardcore band, in the same run of releases.

eras.title: Zeppelin, a dead van and one last record
eras.text: Coalesce made a covers record for a Boston label, watched its tour die on the road, then owed Relapse a record. The result was the shortest and strangest thing in the catalog.

years.cap: Cover art directed by Aaron Turner
years.h: Seven Led Zeppelin covers for Hydra Head Records
years.p: Recorded in September 1998 at Red House and released by Aaron Turner's Hydra Head. Steineger says it was a way to connect with his father, a [[Led Zeppelin|678d88b2-87b0-403b-b63d-5da7465aecc3]] fan.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the release to May 18, 1999 and credits the idea to Metallica's covers work. Hydra Head expanded it in 2007 with re-recorded vocals, new mastering and split tracks from The Get Up Kids and Boy Sets Fire.

Ingram later said the Zeppelin sessions pushed the band toward the groovier feel of its next record.

years.h: The tour van breaks down and Coalesce falls apart again
years.p: Wikipedia and Machine Music say a tour with [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]] and others ended on a broken-down van. Relapse had advanced money for the van, so the band owed the label a record.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia's album article, the van died on a West Coast run in Idaho. Ingram told Machine Music the label advance left the band owing Relapse about $6,000.

The band signed to Relapse Records after Steineger left the Hare Krishna movement, and declined an offer from the Christian label Solid State because the band was too volatile.

years.big: I gave you the money, so give me a record
q: I gave you the money so you're gonna have to give me a record.
years.h: Relapse president Matt Jacobson calls with a debt
years.p: Ingram says the label head told him the $6,000 van advance meant Coalesce still owed Relapse an album. They made it while barely speaking.
years.xp: The music for 0:12 Revolution in Just Listening was composed without Ingram, who arrived later to record vocals on his own. Steineger wrote his guitar parts on an acoustic in about three days, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: 0:12 Revolution in Just Listening: 24 minutes, made in a weekend
years.p: Recorded at Red House with Ed Rose and released by Relapse on November 16, 1999. Decibel later put it in its Hall of Fame in 2008.

eras.title: The internet remembers
eras.text: Coalesce was dead, but fans traded the records and the band's name kept growing. Ingram put a touring band together and went back into old tapes.

years.h: Ingram sings for The Dillinger Escape Plan at Krazy Fest
years.p: When [[The Dillinger Escape Plan|1bc41dff-5397-4c53-bb50-469d2c277197]]'s vocalist left, Sean Ingram filled in at Krazy Fest 4 in 2001, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Coalesce tours again, with Cory White in for Steineger
years.p: Ingram says he organized a national tour with guitarist Cory White of The Esoteric after web interest surged, then regretted not waiting for Jes Steineger.

years.h: Give Them Rope gets a remix as Give Them Rope, She Said
years.p: Edison Recordings reissued the album remastered and remixed, with new artwork, after the band had spent 2002 to 2004 reworking it.

eras.title: Back for good reasons
eras.text: A Hellfest booking pulled Steineger back in, and Coalesce returned on its own terms, with a new drummer, a new sound and a full-length on Relapse.

years.h: Hellfest canceled, so Coalesce plays club shows instead
years.p: The Trenton, NJ festival fell through over legal problems. The band, with Steineger back and Nathan Richardson on drums, played Philadelphia and Wilkes-Barre venues instead.

years.h: Salt and Passage: first new songs in years
years.p: A 7-inch with hand-screened gatefold cover, released on September 11, 2007, with "Son of Son of Man" and "I Am This".

years.h: Ox is the first full-length in a decade
years.p: Recorded at Blacklodge in early 2009, produced by Ed Rose, and released by Relapse on June 9. It leans on Americana, Spaghetti Westerns and bluegrass, per Wikipedia, and reached No. 28 on the Top Heatseekers chart.
years.xp: Nathan Richardson played drums. Ingram also said the band wanted to do it without an outside entity funding it.

years.h: Coalesce announces a break to focus on personal lives
years.p: Wikipedia records the announcement of an indefinite pause, just a year after Ox.

q: I'm trying to un-Lucas-ify this thing as much as possible.
years.src: NPR: A Tale of Two Ropes
years.h: Two mixes of one record, no verdict
years.p: Relapse's two-disc Give Them Rope puts the 1997 mix beside the 2004 remaster and restores the original title, after Ingram found original DAT tapes in his basement.

years.h: Coalesce plays Lawrence with Converge, Torche and Kvelertak
years.p: The last show for twelve years, at the Granada Theatre, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: The reunion and its complications
eras.text: Coalesce came back for one festival and a few shows, with a new drummer, then lost its guitarist to controversy.

years.h: Coalesce reunites for Furnace Fest after twelve years
years.p: The announcement came in February, and by September they opened for Chat Pile in Lawrence with Jeff Gensterblum on drums.

years.h: Jes Steineger steps down; European tour and Roadburn canceled
years.p: Stereogum reported allegations from a former student at the university where he taught, and Steineger said he was stepping down. The band canceled its European dates.
years.xp: Stereogum reported that the band initially said it stood behind Steineger after reviewing evidence, and that the student disputed the band's account. Steineger said the attention had become too heavy a burden.

sources.title: NPR: A Tale Of Two Ropes
